summary.headline: Ambuja Q1 FY27: operating EBITDA INR1,589 crore (16.7% margin, +331 bps QoQ), net cost INR4,241/t, down INR206/t QoQ; trade volumes -2% YoY.
summary.overview: Management reported revenue of about INR9,500 crore, operating EBITDA of INR1,589 crore, and PAT of INR660 crore for Q1 FY27, with EBITDA per ton of INR931 (grey cement INR911). Net operating cost fell INR206/t sequentially to INR4,241/t, which management says is on track for the INR4,250/t full-year guidance despite about INR110/t West Asia-related inflation. Volumes fell sharply: total volume was down about 7% YoY, trade down 2% and non-trade down 21%, as the company deliberately exited low-margin volumes, mainly in South and at acquired assets. Management guided to 8% trade volume growth for FY27 and said July trade volumes were up 8% YoY.

financial_highlights.change: down INR206/t QoQ; FY27 guidance INR4,250/t

financial_highlights.value: down about 7% YoY (per analyst question, not disputed)

financial_highlights.change: trade share of sales 78% vs 74% prior quarter

financial_highlights.value: about 45 crore units; revenue about INR140 crore
financial_highlights.change: Q4 FY26: about 24 crore units, about INR70 crore

financial_highlights.value: Lower in Q1 due to merger true-up; run rate to stay at Q4-level

segments.name: Trade / non-trade
segments.commentary: Trade share rose to 78% from 74%; premium products are 34% of trade sales. Trade volume -2% YoY, non-trade -21% YoY.

segments.name: North
segments.commentary: Highest EBITDA cluster per management; trade volumes grew 2% YoY while low-margin non-trade fell sharply.

segments.name: West
segments.commentary: Trade and non-trade both grew positively per management; Mumbai and Gujarat carry higher-margin non-trade volumes.

segments.name: South
segments.commentary: Deliberate exit of about 1 million tonnes of low or negative EBITDA volume; highest decline in the region. Trade sales only recently started picking up.

segments.name: Central / East
segments.commentary: Central: volumes declined as blended cement was pushed for margin. East: trade volumes sustained with healthy margins.

segments.name: RMC
segments.commentary: RMC EBITDA about INR33 crore in Q1, versus margins of about 14-15% in the prior four quarters; management cited raw material pricing and lease accounting.

guidance_outlook: FY27 net cost guidance INR4,250/t, reaffirmed; management expects INR130-150/t of savings from initiatives, against a possible INR100/t rise in Q2 from geopolitical pressure.
FY27 trade volume growth guidance of 8%, with trade expected to be upwards of 75% of sales; July trade volumes up 8% YoY.
Capacity to reach about 119 Mt by end FY27 (adding about 10.2 Mt), then 8-10 Mt of organic additions per year; FY28 capex in a run rate of INR6,000-7,000 crore.
FY28 green power share targeted at 60% (about 48% on combined sales-plus-consumption basis); RE capacity 1,122 MW by FY28.
Target cost of INR4,000/t or below by end FY28 (about INR250/t further reduction).
capex_capacity: Capacity 109 Mt today; trial runs at Dahej (1.2 Mt expansion) and Salai Banwa, UP (2.4 Mt) have started; Jodhpur (2 Mt commissioned, 3 Mt clinker trials) to stabilise in Q2 and be treated as commissioned in the September quarter.

Kalamboli, Mumbai (1 Mt) and Warisaliganj, Bihar (2.4 Mt) expected in Q2 (Warisaliganj likely September); Bhatinda (1.2 Mt) commissioned; Maratha clinker line moved to Q1 FY28; Mundra expected in about 18-24 months.
RE capacity 973 MW (about 1,122 MW target); WHRS 228 MW rising to about 376 MW; power cost reduced to about INR4.9/kWh from INR5.9.
About 3.5 Mt of old ACC capacity temporarily suspended for about six months; not permanent closure, per management.
Sanghi jetty and clinker expansion about INR600 crore; Penna AFR and WHRS investments INR100-150 crore; first coal block about 30 months away.
demand_pricing: Management said cement demand was stable in Q1, supported by infrastructure and housing; diesel shortages, packing material issues and East/West logistics disruptions hit Q1 volumes.
NSP rose sequentially but fell YoY; management attributed this to Incoterm/ex-works changes and netting of certain channel costs, and said NSP is market-driven.
Analyst comparison: Ambuja NSP about INR100 below UltraTech's reported NSP in Q1, against an average premium of about INR50 over the prior quarters.
Management said Q2 net cost would be slightly better than the June-quarter level, after allowing for part of the geopolitical cost impact.

qa_highlights.question: Will volumes be muted in FY27 given the value-over-volume approach, and can lost Q1 share be recovered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident of 8% trade volume growth on July momentum (+8% YoY); it said share was sustained or improved in trade and was deliberately reduced in non-trade.

qa_highlights.question: What is the economics of green power sales and when will it be consumed in-house?
qa_highlights.answer: About 45 crore units sold in Q1; management expects about 50% consumed in Q2 (about 20 crore units). Grid power costs INR7-8/unit versus green power savings, and at most 10% will be sold going forward.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the INR206/t cost decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited fly ash sourcing, RE power, clinker factor (down about 2-3%), logistics (-INR10/t) and fixed cost optimisation; gross savings were about INR316/t after absorbing INR110/t of West Asia inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ASP up only marginally QoQ and below peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited accounting netting of certain expenses against NSP, ex-works Incoterm effects, and a Q1 disruption; it expects NSP to move in line with industry.

qa_highlights.question: Acquired assets (Penna, Sanghi, Orient): what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Orient at 87% utilisation with minimal investment; Penna needs about INR100-150 crore and a channel push in the South; Sanghi investing INR600 crore in a jetty and improving utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Ambuja-level ICD given to the parent?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described it as part of the MSA arrangement, with Ambuja supplying about 3 Mt of cement to ACC; the ICDs are at 8% coupon and within approved limits, and merger is in advanced stages.

risks_watch: Trade volumes still negative YoY in Q1; the 8% FY27 growth target implies a steep ramp (about 12-13% growth in the remaining nine months per analyst math).
Q2 cost pressure from geopolitical escalation (possible INR100/t rise); clinker and coal inventories give about one month and three months of cover respectively.
Suspended capacity (about 3.5 Mt) and South volume exits (about 1 Mt); restart timing and the impact on fixed-cost absorption remain open.
Maintenance cost accounting: management is still engaging auditors on spreading O&M cost across four quarters; Q1 reflected actuals.
Green power consumption depends on grid connectivity for some plants, expected in two to three quarters; RMC margin fell to about 7% from 14-15%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on cost and capacity delivery, with specific numbers for savings and commissioning, but noticeably defensive on volume decline and NSP gap versus peers, attributing both to one-off disruptions and accounting netting. Several answers on ICDs, RMC margin, cost reconciliation and the Orient valuation were deferred offline.
key_quotes: Our strategy remains clear and consistent, creating sustainable value ahead of volume.
And I would not shy highlighting that we are already seeing an 8% improvement on the trade volumes.
Having a sustainable performance matters more than anything.
Yes, you might be leaving the volume, but you're not leaving value on the table.

growth.why: Guides 8% FY27 trade volume growth (July trade up 8% YoY) and capacity rising to 119 Mt by end FY27 from 109 Mt, with Dahej and Salai Banwa in trials and Jodhpur, Kalamboli and Warisaliganj due in Q2; Q1 total volume was down about 7% YoY and utilisation is only about 65%, so backing is partial.
